case_number: CIVIL APPEAL NO. 2892 OF 2022 [Arising out of SLP(C) No. 4618 of 2021]

parties.respondent: KARNATAKA AYURVEDA MEDICAL COLLEGE AND OTHERS

summary: Dispute over denial of permission for Post-Graduate Ayurvedic courses for 2018-19 academic year due to non-compliance with 2016 Regulations mandating Central Research Laboratory and Animal House facilities. Karnataka High Court allowed writ petition relying on prior judgments granting automatic benefit of subsequent-year permissions to previous year. Supreme Court examined validity of 'subsequent permission retroactivity' doctrine against statutory minimum standards requirements under Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970 and regulations framing.
legal_provisions_cited: Indian Medicine Central Council (Post-Graduate Ayurveda Education) Regulations, 2012
Indian Medicine Central Council (Post-Graduate Ayurveda Education) Regulations, 2016
Section 36(j) of Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970
Sections 13A-13C of Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970
Bahubali Vidyapeeths JV Mandal Gramin Ayurvedic Medical College v. Union of India
Central Council of Indian Medicine v. Union of India
Ayurved Shastra Seva Mandal and Another v. Union of India and Others (2013) 16 SCC 696
final_judgment: Leaving open legal question about retroactive application of subsequent-year permissions, court upheld High Court's practical solution protecting admitted students while remanding matter for fresh consideration of statutory compliance without prejudice to future academic years.
